name: Puah
overview: Puah is a female Hebrew midwife mentioned in the book of Exodus. She is noted for her role during the early period of Israelite slavery in Egypt, where she served as a midwife. Beyond her unique attribute, Scripture does not provide additional details about her tribe or other personal notes.
namesAndTitles: The name Puah is a proper name found in Exodus 1:15. It possibly means "girl," though this meaning is not definitively established. The name itself does not carry a specific title or additional meaning beyond its identification of this individual.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Puah beyond her identity as a Hebrew midwife. There are no listed relatives or connections detailed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Puah is significant in the biblical narrative as one of the Hebrew midwives who played a crucial role during a time when Pharaoh commanded the death of Hebrew male infants. Her actions contributed to the preservation of the Israelite people, demonstrating courage and faithfulness under oppression. This highlights God's providential care for His chosen people through individuals like Puah.
